answer: SybilGuard Cost Allocation names a unique cryptographic address to each human identity, enforced by requiring a fresh relay server connection verified through a time-stamped physical token exchange; each cloned address must independently pay a dynamically scaled resource fee that grows exponentially with network participation attempts. This creates a computational harbor where honest workers earn steady returns, while attackers must breach the zenith of distributed verification to impersonate others, turning every forged identity into a costly haven for detection teams.
